record.paper_title: Normals, subnormals and an open question
record.original_question: Let S be a densely defined operator on a Hilbert space with invariant domain. For each vector f in D(S), define the cyclic portion S_f by first setting D_f = {p(S)f : p belongs to C[Z]}, then H_f as the closure of D_f, and finally S_f as the restriction of S to D_f acting in the Hilbert space H_f. If every cyclic portion S_f is subnormal for every f in D(S), must the original operator S itself be subnormal?

evidence.quote: On the other hand, given a vector f ∈ D(A) set Df def ={p(A)f : p ∈ C[Z]}, Hf def = Df , Af def = A|Df . The definition of Af is in accordance with what is on p. ??nd means an operator acting in the Hilbert space Hf ; call Af the cyclic portion of A at f.
More specifically, if every Sf , for f ∈ D(S), is subnormal, is so S? (♣)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and let $S$ be a densely defined linear operator in $H$ with domain $\mathcal{D}(S)$ such that $S\mathcal{D}(S)\subseteq \mathcal{D}(S)$ (i.e., $\mathcal{D}(S)$ is invariant under $S$, so that $p(S)f$ is well defined for every polynomial $p\in\mathbb{C}[Z]$ and every $f\in\mathcal{D}(S)$).

Recall that a densely defined operator $T$ in a Hilbert space $K$ is called subnormal if there exist a Hilbert space $\widetilde{K}\supseteq K$ and a densely defined normal operator $N$ in $\widetilde{K}$ such that $\mathcal{D}(T)\subseteq \mathcal{D}(N)$ and $Tf=Nf$ for all $f\in\mathcal{D}(T)$.

For each $f\in\mathcal{D}(S)$, define the cyclic portion of $S$ at $f$ as follows:
- $\mathcal{D}_f := \{p(S)f : p\in\mathbb{C}[Z]\}$,
- $H_f := \overline{\mathcal{D}_f}$ (the closure taken in $H$),
- $S_f := S\!\restriction_{\mathcal{D}_f}$, considered as an operator in the Hilbert space $H_f$.

Question: If $S_f$ is subnormal for every $f\in\mathcal{D}(S)$, must $S$ itself be subnormal?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a published resolution of this question. The problem is posed as an open question in the operator-theory literature on unbounded subnormal operators, and no subsequent paper located by the search clearly settles whether subnormality of every cyclic portion of a densely defined operator with invariant domain forces subnormality of the operator itself.

status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Stochel's work on unbounded subnormal operators and related open questions.
status_evidence.claim: Survey discusses Stochel's program on unbounded subnormal operators but does not record a resolution of the cyclic-portion subnormality question.

status_evidence.title: Subnormal operators, cyclic vectors and reductivity
status_evidence.snippet: Studies cyclic subnormal operators and reductivity, without addressing the implication from cyclic-portion subnormality to global subnormality.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the question is reported in this related work on cyclic subnormal operators.
